name: Baby Pink
lede: Baby Pink is a pale, soft pink, named for the nursery.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines baby pink simply as a pale pink [1]. The name is recorded in several systems: Ridgway's 1912 standard, ISCC-NBS blocks 4 and 28, and Maerz and Paul, whose merged entries carry first-recorded dates of 1884, 1912 and 1928 [2]. Wikipedia cites the ISCC-NBS system for its swatch [2].

Its neighbors include Tea Rose, Chatenay Pink and Spanish Pink, all within a few units of distance [2]. The name does not record when pink became linked to babies [1]. Next to [[pink]] and [[rose-pink]], it is the palest of the family [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 15 paintings in our archive of 23,781 match this color, 0.06% of them, as photographed [3]. The earliest match is dated 1400, 484 years before the earliest record in our sources (1884), so it is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not proof of the pigment or dye [2][3]. In printed English the word peaks in the 2010s [3].

origin.named_after: the pale pink of infant clothing
